newsitem.title: FRANCE: CYCLING-OLANO SNATCHES LEAD ONE DAY FROM FINISH.
newsitem.headline: CYCLING-OLANO SNATCHES LEAD ONE DAY FROM FINISH.

text.p: Spain's Abraham Olano snatched overall leadership in the Dauphine Libere from Russian Vyachelav Yekimov when he won the sixth stage on Saturday.
Olano took the 187 km leg from Digne-les-Bains ahead of German Udo Bolts, with Frenchman Jean-Cyril Robin third.
Yekimov, who had taken first place from Briton Chris Boardman on Tuesday's second stage, lost ground on the tough climb at Izoard and finished four minutes nine seconds behind Olano.
Boardman, who has struggled with fitness and technical problems, did not complete the stage and puled out after 81 km at Barcelonette.
Switzerland's Olympic road race champion Pascal Richard, who in mid-March suffered a bad accident while training, was a non-starter.
Sunday's seventh and final stage to Chambery is punctuated by four climbs.
